headline: 2 contracts catalogued on Robinhood Chain (1 Fables hook, 1 Uniswap v4 PoolManager); Fables' own address page was not retrievable, so coverage is thin.

findings.text: The Robinhood Chain explorer is robinhoodchain.blockscout.com (per chainlist and Robinhood support search results). No name-tag search page was fetched, because the fetch budget ran out. Addresses came from search-grounded results instead; no Etherscan-family explorer applies to this chain.

Fables' deployed-contracts page is listed as https://www.fables.fi/docs/addresses in the candydrops article's sources. Fetching it returned only the homepage meta shell, with no address content. docs_url and deployed_contracts_doc are therefore set from those listings, not from a retrieved address table.

No audit links were pinned. The GitHub README says 'Not yet externally audited'. A third-party article (candydrops) says there is no Fables-specific audit report, and says parent Alphix was audited by Sherlock in Dec 2025. No audit PDF was available to read, so no in-scope addresses were extracted.

The github.com/FablesFi/fables repo was fetched. The root listing shows lib, licenses, src, test, README and foundry.toml, with no deployments or broadcast folder. The README lists the hook builds and the AccessManager role model, but no deployed addresses. No commit SHA could be pinned from the page.
Only one chain (Robinhood Chain, id 4663) is in scope. All addresses are recorded against it.
No factory contract was identified. The README says one hook serves many pools, and pools live inside the Uniswap v4 PoolManager singleton, so there is no factory enumeration view to read.

Roles were assigned tentatively: the FablesRWA hook as 'other (hook)' and the Uniswap v4 PoolManager as 'other (holds all funds)'. The repo README documents an OpenZeppelin AccessManager (roles ADMIN, FEE_POKER, PAUSER, DISCOUNT_ADMIN, REVENUE_OPS, SEEDER), but its address was not found.

Only addresses that appear in a search-result page body are in admin_addresses[], without fetched_at. The $FABLES token address appeared only in an X search snippet (the X page was blocked on fetch), so it is in unknowns[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery slice, so grade is unknown. The Fables site, GitHub repo, iq.wiki and candydrops pages were fetched, and four search passes were run. Two addresses were catalogued; the AccessManager and the other hooks, markets and token were not located.

evidence.shows: Official site. Describes a dynamic-fee ve(3,3) exchange on Uniswap v4, live on Robinhood Chain. The fetch returned only meta tags (no body), and no addresses appear.

Fetch of the docs addresses page returned only the homepage meta shell, with no contract addresses. The URL was named in the candydrops source list (derived: the page is presumed to be the official contract list but its content could not be read).

Official Fables hooks repo. The README gives chain id 4663, six hook builds, hooks 'immutable (no proxy, no upgrade)', and AccessManager roles. It says 'Not yet externally audited' and gives security@fables.fi as the security contact. The root listing has no deployments file. License is BUSL-1.1.

Third-party wiki. Describes Fables as a non-custodial Uniswap v4 hook DEX on Robinhood Chain. It cites the docs URLs www.fables.fi/docs, /docs/fables-and-ve33 and /docs/providing-liquidity. The fee-setting and FABLES token roadmap details are secondary-source claims.

Third-party article. Says the operator is Alphix Association (Zug), the chain is id 4663, and nine markets are live. It states there is no Fables-specific audit and that parent Alphix was audited by Sherlock in Dec 2025. Its sources list names www.fables.fi/docs/addresses, /docs/security and /docs/tokenomics.

Search-result page body (not directly fetched). A Uniswap hooklist bot PR labels 0x5eb87f69be00df39981622fd60a8de4b7837e080 on Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663) as 'FablesRWA', a session-aware dynamic-fee hook for tokenized equity pools. Affiliation with Fables is inferred from the name, which matches the repo's calendar-fee hook.

Search-result page body (not directly fetched). Lists the Uniswap v4 PoolManager on Robinhood Chain as 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, described as the chain-wide v4 singleton. Also gives the explorer as robinhoodchain.blockscout.com.

Search-result page body (not directly fetched). Independently lists the same PoolManager address 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951 as the Uniswap v4 singleton. The Fables README says this PoolManager holds all Fables funds.
Search-result page body (not directly fetched). Robinhood Chain id 4663 uses robinhoodchain.blockscout.com as its explorer.

unknowns: D1: robinhoodchain.blockscout.com name-tag search was not fetched (tool-call budget exhausted; no explorer search URL was in the allowlist). The Fables AccessManager, the other hooks and the per-market pools were not located.

D1-offchain: no on-chain read was performed this run. No address was pinned, and surfacer URLs for discovered addresses would be rejected by the allowlist. Pages that returned only an empty shell: https://www.fables.fi/docs/addresses. Pages blocked: x.com/fablesfi (permission denied) and docs.fables.fi (allowlist rejection).

D2: the contents of https://www.fables.fi/docs/addresses (named in a third-party source list) could not be read. The full address list with roles for the hooks, AccessManager, ledger and markets is still missing. Next run should fetch it now that the URL has appeared in a fetched result.

D3: no Fables-specific audit exists per the README and a third-party article. The Sherlock Dec 2025 audit of parent Alphix is reported by candydrops only, with no report URL. Not walked; no audit-era addresses.

D4: the FablesFi/fables repo shows no deployments or broadcast artifacts in the root listing. The test/fork folder and the docs may contain addresses; subfolders were not walked and no commit SHA was pinned.

D5: chain Robinhood Chain: only 2 addresses surfaced, from the Uniswap hooklist PR (FablesRWA hook) and from Bitquery and Bags docs (PoolManager). Sources tried: fables.fi, GitHub, iq.wiki, candydrops, web search.

D6: no factory identified; one hook is described as serving many pools. Pool enumeration via PoolManager events or the Fables API was not attempted. Nine markets are reported (ETH/USDG, GLD/USDG, SPY/USDG, NVDA/USDG, TSLA/USDG, META/USDG and others), and their pool IDs were not retrieved.

D7: the AccessManager address (OpenZeppelin, governs ADMIN, FEE_POKER, PAUSER and other roles) and the ADMIN holder (EOA or multisig) were not found. A third-party repo (gamween/clim-fables) references the deployed ETH/USDG hook and AccessManager, but that page was not fetched and gives no usable address.

D8: $FABLES token address 0xb63d07CEf74bE747231d601bb2FAa6B252c68106 appears only in a search snippet of x.com/fablesfi, which was not fetchable, so it is excluded from admin_addresses. It is unverified and should be checked on Blockscout. The PROLOGUE pre-token address was not found.

D8: other hooks (FablesHook, FablesHookETH, Exclusive, StableHookLite builds) and the ETH/USDG hook have no addresses recorded. Only the FablesRWA hook surfaced, via the Uniswap hooklist bot. Its mapping to a specific Fables build is unconfirmed.

protocol_metadata.about: Fables is a Uniswap v4 hook-based exchange on Robinhood Chain where liquidity providers deposit into pair-specific concentrated-liquidity markets (e.g. tokenized stocks, ETFs and ETH paired with USDG) and receive ERC-6909 ledger receipts. Its distinctive mechanism is a dynamic swap fee set by an on-chain trading calendar, a flat autonomous fee, or bounded expiring off-chain overrides. Gauge staking and ve(3,3) emissions are described as part of the design. The README states the hooks are immutable and access control is an OpenZeppelin AccessManager; the repo is not yet externally audited.
